schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE R (A INT, B INT);
q1: SELECT X.A, SUM(X.A + X.B) FROM R AS X GROUP BY X.A
q2: SELECT Y.A, SUM(Y.A + Y.B) FROM R AS Y GROUP BY Y.A
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT X.A, SUM(X.A + X.B) FROM R AS X GROUP BY X.A
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT Y.A, SUM(Y.A + Y.B) FROM R AS Y GROUP BY Y.A
explanation: Both queries, Q1 and Q2, are semantically equivalent. They both select column A from table R and calculate the sum of the values of A and B for each unique value of A, grouping the results by A. The difference in the alias names (X in Q1 and Y in Q2) does not affect the semantics of the query.
